notes: [P1] outcome/brief-conflict: the acceptance criterion says `npm test` passes "with no existing test file edited", but the diff edits test/card-buttons.test.js, test/pause-speed.test.js, test/sell.test.js and test/upgrade.test.js. Each now sets Math.random to return 0 while it imports src/main.js, so the opening round lands on path 1. The edits cannot be avoided: the brief also requires src/main.js to open with pickPath(Math.random), and these four tests boot main.js and click cells laid out for path 1. Without the edits they would pass or fail depending on the random path. The brief's own touches list names all four files, so the signer expected these edits. Each edit is small and puts Math.random back in a finally block. I am filing this as a follow-up for the brief's internal conflict, not as a defect in the diff.

[P2] test-coverage: random-path.test.js checks nextRound and pickPath on their own, but no test drives src/main.js through a won or lost round to confirm that a click calls nextRound with Math.random (rather than restart) and redraws the path. That wiring is only checked by reading the code.

[P2] robustness: pickPath trusts `random` to return a value in [0, 1). A value of 1 or more, or below 0, makes it return undefined, and createGame then fails later and further from the cause. Math.random never does this and the brief defines the contract this way, so this is a nice-to-have guard only.
